speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent head injuries, headaches, or visual disturbances? I also need to know if you have a history of cancer or recent infections, as these could point to an underlying cause for these neurological changes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of cancer, HIV, or recent travel to areas with endemic infections? I also need to know if you have experienced any seizures or changes in your level of consciousness.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of non-compliant HIV treatment, I suspect an opportunistic infection like toxoplasmosis or a primary CNS lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast.

text: The MRI findings of disseminated, non-enhancing white matter lesions in an HIV-positive patient are highly suggestive of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Do you have any history of recent weight loss or fever, and have you noticed any changes in your speech or vision?

speaker: Doctor
